title: Millaisia and minkälaisia: describing several things
summary: Use millaisia or minkälaisia to ask for qualities of the members of an ordinary plural group: Millaisia kirjat ovat? Millaisia talot ovat? — Talot ovat pieniä.
targetSkills: Millaisia and minkälaisia: describing several things
prerequisiteSkills: Millainen and minkälainen: describing one person or thing
objectives: Ask about an ordinary plural group's qualities with millaisia or minkälaisia.
Describe the group's members with a plural partitive adjective.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.
Use millaisia or minkälaisia to ask for qualities of the members of an ordinary plural group: Millaisia kirjat ovat? (“What are the books like?”). The subject noun has its plural basic form.
keyPoints: Do not use singular millainen for the taught plural description pattern.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: The description normally uses the plural partitive: Kirjat ovat hyviä (“The books are good”). This lesson uses ordinary groups of separate things, not every exceptional plural predicate pattern. The supplied forms show pieni → pieniä, hyvä → hyviä, uusi → uusia and suuri → suuria.
A natural short reply to “Millaisia talot ovat?” is “Pieniä.” (“Small.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
The supplied eivät ole makes the statement negative. Both descriptions still use the plural partitive for the members of these ordinary groups.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Use the plural partitive adjective when describing the members of these ordinary groups.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: pieniä means small here. Pieni has the taught plural partitive pieniä; add -ä to this surface pattern.
hyviä means good here. Hyvä changes final ä to i and adds ä for plural partitive hyviä.
uusia means new here. Uusi has the taught plural partitive uusia.
suuria means large here. Suuri has the taught plural partitive suuria; add -a to this surface pattern.
ystävällisiä means friendly here. Ystävällinen changes -nen to -siä: ystävällisiä.
vanhoja means old here. Vanha changes final a to o and adds -ja: vanhoja.

examples.finnish: Talot eivät ole suuria. Talot ovat pieniä.
examples.english: The houses are not large. The houses are small.
steps: Talot: houses; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Talo + plural -t gives talot.
eivät: do not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). Eivät is the plural third-person negative verb.
ole: be; main verb after the negative verb. After a present-tense negative verb, olla takes the unchanged form ole.
suuria: large; description of what the subject is like. Suuri has the taught plural partitive suuria; add -a to this surface pattern.
